report:
## Conclusion

**The claim is accurate.** Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years. This is confirmed directly by the FDA-approved product labeling.

According to the FDA's official prescribing information on DailyMed, "Kyleena is a progestin-containing intrauterine system (IUS) indicated for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years" (dailymed.nlm.nih.gov). The original FDA approval label from 2016 states the same: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years" (accessdata.fda.gov). Kyleena received FDA approval on September 16, 2016, based on a Phase III clinical trial in 1,452 women aged 18–35, demonstrating a Pearl Index of 0.29 after five years and greater than 99% efficacy per year of use (drugs.com history page).

It's worth noting that Kyleena is one of several levonorgestrel-releasing IUDs marketed by Bayer and others, each with different approved durations: Skyla is approved for 3 years, Kyleena for 5 years, and Mirena/Liletta for 8 years, reflecting differences in hormone dose and device size (drugs.com "Difference Between Kyleena, Liletta, Skyla, Mirena"). This distinction is important for accuracy but does not undermine the specific claim about Kyleena's 5-year approval.

**Sources:**
1. https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080
2. https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf
3. https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html
4. https://www.drugs.com/medical-answers/difference-kyleena-liletta-skyla-mirena-3172659/
